h1:
10 Most Popular Restaurants
in Prachuap Khiri Khan
intro: Prachuap Khiri Khan is a province where the sea is always close — which means fish and crab arrive at the table fresh on the same day. We've picked 10 restaurants that locals here actually eat at, from fresh seafood along Khlong Waan beach, Hua Hin boat noodles, and old-school coffee at Cafe Jek Pia, to seaside cafés at Pak Nam Pran. A mix of restaurants with decades of history and beautiful-view spots worth visiting at least once.
chips: 🦐 Fresh seafood right on the beach

blocks.html:
When most people think of Prachuap Khiri Khan, Hua Hin and the long beach strip comes to mind. But the real character of this province runs all the way down the coast — from Ao Prachuap and Khlong Waan to Pak Nam Pran and all the way south to Bang Saphan. Fishing boats come in every morning and the fish, crab, squid, and shellfish are on tables the same day. Each area has its own personality: Pak Nam Pran is a fishing village where seafood restaurants line the beach, Hua Hin has the old town with its Chinese-heritage atmosphere and old-school coffee shops, while Ao Prachuap and Bang Saphan offer home-style seafood at prices that feel genuinely generous, right by the sea. Eating here always feels like a proper break.

Several restaurants on this list have been part of the province for a long time. Cafe Jek Pia in Hua Hin is a 70–80-year-old wooden coffee house so associated with the intersection out front that locals just call it "the Jek Pia intersection." Udom Phochana in Pak Nam Pran has been open for over 60 years and is considered the original sun-dried squid restaurant in Thailand. Khrua Jae Maew draws queues because its yellow curry crab and crab-roe relish are talked about constantly. For view seekers, Ao Takiab Seafood and I Talay Bang Saphan both sit right on the beach, where you eat with the sound of waves beside you. For noodle lovers, Jae Din's braised beef boat noodles have been a Hua Hin legend for generations. And for a slow seaside coffee, Cha Bar Coffee at Pak Nam Pran is the natural answer. Pick your spot and go.

blocks.name: Khon Kin Pla
blocks.area: Khlong Waan sub-district, Mueang Prachuap Khiri Khan District, Prachuap Khiri Khan Province
blocks.signature: Steamed milkfish (pla nuanjhan) in soy sauce, bone-removed; deep-fried spotted mackerel in fish sauce; sea crab stir-fried with cha-khram leaves
blocks.descHtml:
Drive south along the coast from Prachuap town toward Khlong Waan and you want fresh, home-style sea fish without dressing up? "Khon Kin Pla" is the name people think of first. The restaurant is in the Pom Tamruat–Nong Hin lane, about 200 metres south of the Khlong Waan pier near the Trichewa Hotel. It has been a local regular and a traveller stopover for years. Works well for families or friend groups who want a relaxed waterside table and a spread of fish to share.

The hero dish is "steamed milkfish (pla nuanjhan) in soy sauce, bone-removed" — the signature fish of the province, with the bones carefully removed at the table before serving, making it easy to eat. Multiple reviews call it a dish you have to try. Another table-standard is "deep-fried spotted mackerel (pla inthari) in fish sauce" — firm, sweet flesh, crisp skin, drizzled in house fish sauce. Then there's "sea crab stir-fried with cha-khram leaves" — pairing the coastal herb cha-khram with sea crab, a fragrance you won't find at many other restaurants.

The atmosphere is a wooden waterside restaurant with private pavilion tables — sea breeze, fish visible in the water below. Easy parking. Prices around 251–500 THB per person — midrange for a seafood restaurant given the freshness and the bone-removal service. Reviews score it around 3.8 out of 5 and the consistent praise is for fresh fish, firm flesh, no bones, and a warm and chatty team.

Good to know: several reviews mention food can be slow because the kitchen cooks dishes individually fresh. If coming in a large group or during busy hours, leave extra time. Book ahead or call if you're coming in a bigger party. Open daily from mid-morning through evening. The ideal time is late afternoon arriving in time to watch the sun drop over the sea.
mustOrder: Steamed milkfish in soy sauce, bone-removed
Deep-fried spotted mackerel in fish sauce
Sea crab stir-fried with cha-khram leaves

blocks.name: Chao Le Seafood
blocks.area: Hua Hin, Prachuap Khiri Khan Province
blocks.signature: Sea bass steamed with lime and chili, yellow curry crab, stir-fried squid with salted egg yolk
blocks.descHtml:
When it comes to seafood restaurants that have been part of Hua Hin for a long time, "Chao Le Seafood" is one of the first names that surfaces. The restaurant sits on a wooden deck extended out over the sea on Naretdamri Road, near the night market, walkable from the older hotel district. The standout is eating seafood while listening to waves and feeling the sea breeze throughout the day. Works well for families or groups visiting Hua Hin who want a proper sea-fresh meal without worrying about dress code. Many of the ingredients come from fishing boats docking nearby each day, so the seafood arrives fast from sea to plate.

The most ordered dishes that keep coming up in reviews: steamed sea bass with lime and chili — clean, sour-spicy sauce over fresh fish that reviewers say is consistently good. Yellow curry crab with fragrant curry spice and firm crab meat. Stir-fried squid with salted egg yolk — one of the most popular dishes across many tables. For those who love large prawns, foreign reviewers repeatedly praise the grilled prawns with coconut-peppercorn sauce as something they order again on every visit. The tom yum goong here is rich and deeply flavored — the overall consensus from diners is that the fish is fresh and the dipping and sauce flavors are bold and properly Southern seaside.

Prices are reasonable for the location and the view — roughly 400–600 THB per person. Most reviews say "value is good for the setting." Relaxed atmosphere with wooden tables and open space — not formal, but genuinely feels like eating by the sea. Open daily approximately 10:00–21:30. Popular around sunset when people come for the view.

Good to know: evenings on weekends get busy and parking is somewhat limited. If coming as a large group or wanting a deck-edge table, arrive early or call ahead. Ask the price per weight for fresh items before ordering to keep tabs on the total.
mustOrder: Sea bass steamed with lime and chili
Stir-fried squid with salted egg yolk

blocks.name: Cafe Jek Pia
blocks.area: Hua Hin, Prachuap Khiri Khan Province
blocks.signature: Traditional coffee, Thai iced tea, pork blood soup, khao man kai, pork satay
blocks.descHtml:
Coming to Hua Hin and want to start the morning exactly like a local? Cafe Jek Pia is the first stop any Hua Hin regular would take you to. A 70–80-year-old wooden coffee house at the Soi Hua Hin 57 intersection, in the old town — so deeply associated with this corner that locals call it "the Jek Pia intersection." Perfect for anyone wanting a complete, simple breakfast in one spot, since food carts from neighbouring stalls pull up around the shop and you can order across, all sharing the same tables.

The most ordered items: pork blood soup — clear, rounded broth, served hot; reviewers consistently say drinking it in the morning is deeply satisfying. Khao man kai with tender chicken and sharp dipping sauce. Pork satay, described by many as one of the area's best. And the centrepiece of the shop — traditional coffee and Thai iced tea — ordered with toasted bread as a classic breakfast set. Rich, sweet, and buttery in the old-school coffee-bag style that gets harder to find every year.

The atmosphere is an old wooden building, minimal tables, close quarters. Weekend mornings get packed and sharing a table with strangers is part of the experience — that's the old-style café charm. Very accessible prices — most items 50–100 THB, a full meal for two well under a few hundred baht.

Good to know: the shop opens in two sessions — morning approximately 06:30–12:00 and a short evening round 17:30–19:30. The evening menu differs and adds snacks and some seafood. If you're coming for the full breakfast experience, be there before late morning — popular items sell out fast and the crowd is thickest early. A cross-generation institution in Hua Hin, consistent flavors, and one of the city's most photographed addresses.
blocks.stayLabel: Well-located stays in Prachuap Khiri Khan
blocks.bestFor: First morning breakfast in Hua Hin — early risers

blocks.name: Jae Din Boat Noodles Hua Hin
blocks.area: Hua Hin, Prachuap Khiri Khan Province
blocks.signature: Braised beef boat noodles, dense broth, braised beef kaphrao
blocks.descHtml:
When it comes to legendary boat noodles in Hua Hin, "Jae Din" is one of the first names locals bring up. A small shop in Soi Hua Hin 55/2, across from the Chatchai market, running for over half a century — from Jae Din herself down to the next generation. The point every reviewer agrees on is the dense, rounded broth — gently sweet, lightly salty, with braised beef that's so tender it nearly dissolves. Those who love the bold, original boat noodle style will feel right at home.

The must-order is the braised beef boat noodles and braised pork waterfall noodles — large bowl, generously loaded, satisfying. Another dish that keeps people coming back is the garlic-fried braised pork — crisp outside, tender inside, full of garlic fragrance. Also available: braised beef kaphrao, seafood tom yum noodles, pad thai, and soy-sauce fried noodles. Most reviewers praise the tender, luscious meat and a broth that stays appealing no matter how many times you return.

Very good value — most items under 100 THB, a bowl of noodles running 50–80 THB. Open daily 09:00–16:30. Works well as a late-morning meal or lunch before heading to the Chatchai market. Simple chairs and tables in old-shop style, casual service.

Good to know: the shop is in a narrow lane. Cars can't get in easily and parking is almost nonexistent — most people park on Phetkasem Road and walk in the short distance. The midday period (11:30–13:00) fills up, so arriving slightly earlier or later means a shorter wait. The walk in is more than worth it for a bowl of Hua Hin's most talked-about braised beef boat noodles.
blocks.stayLabel: Well-located stays in Prachuap Khiri Khan
blocks.bestFor: Late-morning or midday meal before exploring the Chatchai market

blocks.name: Khrua Jae Maew Pak Nam Pran
blocks.signature: Yellow curry crab, sun-dried squid, young coconut shoots stir-fried with oyster sauce, clear seafood tom yum
blocks.descHtml:
Coming to Pranburi and wanting seafood the way locals here actually eat it? Khrua Jae Maew Pak Nam Pran is the name that comes up first. Open for nearly 20 years in Soi Phasuk Wanit 8 near Pak Nam Pran — a home-style seafood restaurant with no fancy décor, no air-conditioning, but fresh ingredients every day and cooking that delivers on bold flavors. Works perfectly for families or groups ordering multiple shared dishes.

The dish reviewers consistently point to as a non-negotiable order is the yellow curry crab — firm crab meat in a fragrant yellow curry sauce with just the right heat. Sun-dried squid fried until it's bouncy without being tough, fragrant with garlic. Young coconut shoots stir-fried with oyster sauce bring a natural crunch and sweetness. Clear seafood tom yum — clean, sharp, properly sour-first. Another dish that regulars recommend strongly is the crab-roe chili relish, eaten with fresh vegetables — deeply satisfying and hard to stop eating.

Prices are accessible — stir-fries start in the mid-hundreds of baht, averaging 250–500 THB per person depending on how much crab and prawn you order. The kitchen is large so food comes out relatively quickly. Open daily approximately 10:00–20:00 with parking near the shop, though not spacious.

Good to know: during long weekends or festivals the queue is real — arrive before peak hours or call ahead to book. The lasting popularity comes from consistent ingredient freshness and cooking that doesn't drift. Anyone passing through Pranburi who doesn't stop here is missing a local favourite.
mustOrder: Young coconut shoots stir-fried with oyster sauce
blocks.stayLabel: Well-located stays in Prachuap Khiri Khan
blocks.bestFor: Groups and families — bold and fresh seafood

blocks.title: 🛏️ Stay by the sea and eat your fill
blocks.text: Prachuap is most comfortable to explore when you have a base. Stay in Hua Hin if you want to be close to the old town and popular restaurants; stay in Pranburi if you're planning a seafood run through Pak Nam Pran; or head south to Bang Saphan for a quieter, slower pace by the sea. Book accommodation in advance for long weekends to get better rates and the right location. Wake up to old-school coffee in the morning, sit down with crab and the sound of the waves in the evening — no need to rush home.

blocks.name: Udom Phochana
blocks.area: Pak Nam Pran, Pranburi District, Prachuap Khiri Khan Province
blocks.signature: Sun-dried squid, sea bass fried in fish sauce, grilled prawns, sea bass clear tom yum
blocks.descHtml:
Udom Phochana is a legendary seafood restaurant right on the Pak Nam Pran beach, Prachuap Khiri Khan — open across generations for over 60 years, widely credited as the original sun-dried squid restaurant in Thailand. For anyone driving through Pranburi who wants a big fresh seafood meal right on the beach, this is the address locals and travellers keep coming back to. The restaurant is large with multiple seating zones to choose from, spacious parking out front — works for families and groups.

The must-order is the sun-dried squid — the restaurant's signature item that reviewers mention most. Bouncy-firm when fried, sweet, fragrant. Sea bass fried in fish sauce, perfectly crisp all the way through and soaked in the house fish sauce. Large grilled prawns. Clear sea bass tom yum that many reviewers describe as "generous pieces, fresh, right flavor." The home-style dishes that complement rice have consistent old-hand quality that settles in comfortably. One detail diners keep talking about: every table gets a free side dish and fresh fruit — a small gesture that makes the meal feel worthwhile.

The atmosphere is an open-air restaurant by the beach — some tables so close to the sand you can walk straight onto it from your seat. Sea breeze all day. Prices per person about 251–500 THB — fair for fresh seafood by the sea. Located on Pak Nam Pran Road in Pranburi, open daily 10:30–21:30. A note from reviews: the 4–6pm window is the sweet spot — good views, cool breeze. After dark the beach mosquitoes increase, so bring repellent if you're planning an evening stay.
mustOrder: Sea bass fried in fish sauce
blocks.stayLabel: Well-located stays in Prachuap Khiri Khan
blocks.bestFor: Family or group seafood meal by the beach — afternoon breeze is ideal

blocks.name: Rab Lom Restaurant
blocks.area: Mueang District, Prachuap Khiri Khan Province
blocks.signature: Sun-dried squid, crab omelette, steamed mussels with herbs, seafood tom yum
blocks.descHtml:
Rab Lom is a seasoned seafood restaurant right along the beachfront road of Ao Prachuap Bay — facing the bay directly. Drive along the coastal road and want fresh sea food in a simple, no-fuss setting? This is the natural stop. The standout: eat with your meal, take in the view of the wide bay, and after eating you can walk across the road to digest by the beach. Works well for families and groups wanting seafood without formality.

The most-ordered dishes: sun-dried squid fried crisp outside, tender inside. Fluffy crab omelette packed with crab meat. Herb-steamed mussels. Hot, bold seafood tom yum. For those who want vegetables, morning glory stir-fried with salted fish is popular too. The deep-fried prawn tempura and prawn fish cakes both get consistent praise for crispiness.

Reviews consistently describe fresh ingredients, flavors that hit properly, and good value at about 101–250 THB per person — making it one of Prachuap's most accessible seafood spots. Open-air wooden tables, breeze throughout the day, large bay-side parking lot, and a souvenir shop in front of the restaurant selling Prachuap specialties.

Good to know: open daily approximately 10:00–21:00. Long weekends bring crowds — calling ahead or arriving before peak helps. If you want the best outdoor sea-breeze seating, come for the late afternoon before sunset — you get the atmosphere and the views in their best form. The sunset timing from this spot is hard to beat.
blocks.stayLabel: Well-located stays in Prachuap Khiri Khan
blocks.bestFor: Family seafood meal by the bay
blocks.spice: Some bold dishes (tom yum / curry stir-fry) — adjustable
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: seafood · Andy Li / Wikimedia (CC0)

blocks.name: Ao Takiab Seafood
blocks.signature: Khao phad khot pu (super crab fried rice), sea bass fried in fish sauce, fresh Surat oysters, grilled seafood
blocks.descHtml:
Want to eat Hua Hin seafood with your feet practically in the sand, listening to waves? "Ao Takiab Seafood" is the first name both Hua Hin locals and visitors think of. Located at the end of Ao Hua Don 15 lane right on Khao Takiab beach — an open-air restaurant seating over a hundred people with nearly 180-degree sea views, stretching from Khao Takiab to Khao Tao, with Singha Island and Turtle Island in the middle distance. Works for families, groups of friends, or even company offsite events.

The dish almost every table orders is the "khao phad khot pu" (super crab fried rice) — served hot, fragrant, loaded with crab meat, the restaurant's signature. The other non-negotiable is the sea bass fried in fish sauce — large fish, firm flesh, the house fish sauce served separately for self-drizzling, with a spicy salad dressing and seafood dipping sauce on the side. Fresh Surat oysters the size of your palm, served with a full set of condiments. And the grilled seafood with charcoal fragrance. Salted egg prawn stir-fry and young coconut hor mok are also popular tables-wide orders mentioned across many reviews.

Prices sit at the sea-view restaurant level — 251–500 THB per person, higher if you order large prawns or a lot of crab. Many reviewers note the view justifies the price, though a few feel portions can be on the small side relative to cost. Cash-only at the restaurant. Open-air only — no air-conditioning. Weekends fill up fast. Google rating 4.5 from tens of thousands of reviews is a strong consistent signal.

Open daily approximately 10:30–21:00 Mon–Fri, extended to 22:00 on Sat–Sun. A short drive from central Hua Hin toward Khao Takiab. Parking is available. After eating, you can walk directly onto the beach. For a Hua Hin visit where you want both the seafood and the sea, this is a solid choice.
mustOrder: Khao phad khot pu (super crab fried rice)
Sea bass fried in fish sauce
blocks.stayLabel: Well-located stays in Prachuap Khiri Khan
blocks.bestFor: Family or group seaside seafood meal

blocks.name: I Talay Bang Saphan
blocks.signature: I Talay salad, yam seafood, garlic fried prawns, chili-sauce sea bass
blocks.descHtml:
I Talay Bang Saphan (I TALAY Restaurant) is a seafood restaurant right on Suan Luang Beach — anyone passing through Bang Saphan hears the name early. Located by the sea next to the Coral Bangsaphan Hotel, a short walk from the sand. The restaurant is designed in a modern vintage style with clean white tones, with both air-conditioned indoor sections and an open outdoor section for the sea breeze. A good fit for anyone wanting fresh seafood with a sea view that genuinely delivers. If you're stopping in Bang Saphan and want a reliable meal by the water, this is the reassuring choice.

The most talked-about dish is the "I Talay salad" — the restaurant's own creation: thinly julienned and deep-fried root vegetables (taro, sweet potato, carrot, pumpkin) tossed in a house dressing, crispy and addictive. Multiple reviews mention ordering it again and again. Another popular order: the "yam I Talay" and "yam three friends" (combining prawns, squid, and fried fish roe in one dish) — bold, sour, spicy, and rounded. For main dishes: garlic fried prawns, curry or sour curry with fish, chili-sauce sea bass fried crispy outside and soft inside, and crab roe relish with fresh vegetables. Stir-fried squid with salted egg yolk is also frequently ordered alongside the sea breeze.

Reviews consistently praise fresh ingredients, friendly prices, and a beach atmosphere that feels genuinely good. Many describe the vibe as "feels like a million-dollar setting at accessible prices." Prices around 150–300 THB per person — good value for a beachfront meal. Some reviews note certain dishes lean mild, and food can slow down on busy weekends. Order the signature salad and yam dishes first to make sure you get the standouts.

Open approximately 11:00–24:00, kitchen closes around 22:00, closed Mondays. If you want an evening meal watching the sunset, arrive before dark — you get both the view and the breeze at their best. Address: 135 Moo 9, Phong Prasat sub-district, right on Suan Luang Beach beside the Coral Hotel. What makes this restaurant consistently popular is fresh seafood, reasonable prices, and a genuine beachfront location — a combination that's genuinely rare in Bang Saphan.
blocks.stayLabel: Well-located stays in Prachuap Khiri Khan
blocks.bestFor: Evening beachfront meal watching the sunset — groups and families

blocks.name: Cha Bar Coffee
blocks.signature: Cold Americano, homemade bakery, cakes, brownies, ice cream sundae
blocks.descHtml:
Cha Bar Coffee is a small wooden café on the Pak Nam Pran beachfront — the kind of place you slow down for when you see it driving along Soi Phasuk Wanit 8. An old wooden house renovated into a vintage-feel café, open to the sea breeze with nearly 180-degree ocean views from your seat. Works perfectly for those who want a quiet escape from the rush — couples, photographers, anyone wanting a peaceful working spot by the water. Most reviews say the same thing: "the atmosphere is the hero here." Soft reggae music, warm staff, and you lose track of time.

The most-ordered drink is the cold Americano — aromatic and refreshing with the sea air. For sweeter options the bakery cabinet is full: cakes, brownies, and cold ice cream sundaes that pair perfectly with the view. Popular seasonal items include strawberry cheesecake and butterfly-pea toddy palm cake — subtly sweet, not heavy. For something more unusual there's green tea coffee and macchiato, and a photogenic blue butterfly pea drink. Prices are genuinely accessible — drinks start around 60 THB, cake slices from 90 THB, and a full person per visit runs a couple of hundred baht at most.

Open daily approximately 09:00–18:00. Easy to find on the Pak Nam Pran beachfront road, near seafood restaurants and squid stalls. Good parking. The reason people keep coming back is simple: it's a genuine sea-view café, not just a café with a sea-view photo. Coming for the late afternoon before sunset delivers the best light, the best breeze, and the best moment to sit still for a while. One note: the café is open-air with a smoking area outside. Popular weekends mean the best sea-facing seats fill early — arriving in the morning or before sunset is the smart move.
blocks.stayLabel: Well-located stays in Prachuap Khiri Khan
blocks.bestFor: Slow seaside coffee — watch the sunset

blocks.title: What to know before you eat in Prachuap Khiri Khan

items.title: Getting around
items.text: In Hua Hin, Grab is available and easy to use. But heading out to Khlong Waan, Pak Nam Pran, or Bang Saphan, ride-sharing coverage drops significantly. Renting a car or motorbike is by far the most practical option — many of the seafood restaurants are on beachfronts outside town.

items.title: Carry cash
items.text: Larger restaurants and cafés typically accept QR payment or PromptPay bank transfer. But smaller local shops and old-school coffee houses often take cash only. Keep small bills on hand to avoid any surprises.

items.title: Avoid peak queues
items.text: Popular seafood restaurants like Khrua Jae Maew and Ao Takiab fill fast around midday and 6pm, especially on long weekends. Arriving slightly before or after those windows cuts the wait significantly. Morning spots like Cafe Jek Pia can sell out early — arrive late and you may miss the best items.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: Thai restaurants don't require tips, but leaving spare change or 20–50 THB for good service is always appreciated. Larger restaurants sometimes include a service charge in the bill — check the receipt.

items.title: English menus
items.text: Restaurants in Hua Hin and cafés generally have English menus or photo menus available. Traditional local seafood spots and older restaurants may only have Thai — using Google Translate's camera feature or pointing at food at a nearby table is the practical workaround. Staff are generally friendly.

items.title: Tell them your spice level
items.text: Southern-style food and seafood in this region is genuinely spicy — yam and tom yum dishes carry real heat. If you're chili-sensitive, tell the staff you'd like mild or no chili right when you order. Most kitchens can adjust.

blocks.title: Plan a full eating trip through Prachuap
blocks.html:
With one day to work with, start in Hua Hin with Cafe Jek Pia for old-school coffee and breakfast — the shop opens early and the best items go fast. For lunch, go to Jae Din Boat Noodles in Soi Hua Hin 55/2 for braised beef noodles, then drive south toward Pak Nam Pran for the afternoon.

Make the evening about Pak Nam Pran seafood — Khrua Jae Maew and Udom Phochana are in the same area. If one has a long queue, try the other, which has more seating and a longer history on the beach. Finish the evening with a slow coffee at Cha Bar Coffee on the Pak Nam Pran beachfront. For those heading all the way south to Bang Saphan, I Talay is the beachfront option there — fresh seafood, gentle prices, and a sea view. Budget extra time since seafood is cooked fresh per dish and takes a little longer.

blocks.text: Eating multiple meals here is much easier with a base to stay at. Book a night in Hua Hin, Pranburi, or Bang Saphan — wake up to old-school coffee in the morning, walk to seafood by the sea in the evening, no need to drive home.

faq.q: Which restaurant is the most famous in Prachuap Khiri Khan?
faq.a: Depends on what you're looking for. For seafood, Khrua Jae Maew in Pak Nam Pran is the name most mentioned — the queue is real because the yellow curry crab and crab-roe relish are widely talked about. Ao Takiab Seafood in Hua Hin is famous for the beachfront views and the crab fried rice. For heritage, Cafe Jek Pia in Hua Hin is a 70–80-year-old coffee shop that locals still call the intersection after.

faq.q: What are the signature foods of Prachuap Khiri Khan?
faq.a: This is a long coastal province, so the standouts are all from the sea: sun-dried squid at Rab Lom and Udom Phochana, crab at Khrua Jae Maew, milkfish (pla nuanjhan) bone-removed at Khon Kin Pla in Khlong Waan, and Jae Din's braised beef boat noodles in Hua Hin. Old-school traditional coffee at Cafe Jek Pia is another signature the city is known for.

faq.q: How much does eating at these restaurants cost?
faq.a: It varies quite a bit by type. Old-school coffee at Cafe Jek Pia starts around 50–100 THB. Jae Din Boat Noodles is about 50–80 THB a bowl. Cha Bar café runs 60–120 THB per person. Multi-dish seafood restaurants like Khrua Jae Maew, Udom Phochana, or Ao Takiab typically work out to about 250–500 THB per person for a shared spread.

faq.q: Do these restaurants require advance booking?
faq.a: Popular seafood restaurants during long weekends fill up fast. Khrua Jae Maew, Udom Phochana, and Ao Takiab Seafood all benefit from a call-ahead or early arrival. Rab Lom also takes reservations. Single-dish shops and cafés like Cafe Jek Pia, Jae Din, and Cha Bar are walk-in — no booking needed — but peak times mean waiting.

faq.q: Which restaurants are open for dinner or late night?
faq.a: Most seafood restaurants are open through the evening. Khon Kin Pla in Khlong Waan is open until around 10pm. Ao Takiab Seafood stays open until roughly 10pm. Cafe Jek Pia is morning-focused with a short evening session. Jae Din Boat Noodles and Cha Bar Coffee are daytime spots. For evening seafood plans, the beachfront restaurants are the right choice.
